dispatch_scope: DESCRIPTION sources confirmed by the shipping binary to select Diagram::Deployment. Component and Class dispatches are separate mechanisms.

java_locations.role: Creates a named NOTE Entity through the current quark context, giving it the same immediate parent relation as ordinary leaves.
Creates an attached note Entity in the current group and a hidden note-to-target Link, so the note is owned locally but is not standalone.
Defines the heterogeneous quark-backed child relation and makes a group with any surviving note nonempty.
Emits direct note and ordinary leaves inside their owner cluster and only top-parent leaves in the root stream.
Builds each owner's Magma from immediate unlinked leaves; attached notes and their targets are excluded by the hidden link.

rust_locations.role: Correctly retains DeploymentNote.owner and quark_order, while DeploymentNode.children intentionally stores only ordinary node ids.
The owner-aware leaf order can see notes, but cluster_ids comes only from nonempty node.children and only ordinary child nodes are registered in clusters.
Appends every targetless note to root Magma regardless of owner and never includes direct owned floating notes in an owner-local set.
Traversal, painting and geometry independently recompute the node-children-only cluster predicate, so partial registration would leave inventories inconsistent.

claimed_invariant: Deployment rendering projects one heterogeneous immediate-child relation from ordinary nodes and all laid-out notes. A node is a cluster whenever it has any renderable direct child. Owned notes are solved and painted exactly once inside that cluster with an owner-qualified name. Root and owner-local Magma inventories contain only their immediate unlinked leaves in quark order; attached notes are cluster members but non-standalone because their hidden link touches the note and target.
causal_divergence: DeploymentNote already carries owner and quark_order, but the renderer repeatedly projects cluster identity from DeploymentNode.children alone. Note-only owners collapse to leaf entities; owned notes are omitted from cluster membership and qualified identity; targetless owned notes leak into root Magma; and downstream geometry consumes a different cluster/leaf inventory from SVEK ordering. These symptoms share one missing heterogeneous owner projection.
planned_model_change: Introduce one owner-aware deployment cluster projection derived from ordinary children plus laid-out notes and use it in graph construction, traversal, frame calculation, endpoint adjustment and rectangle recovery. Register every owned laid-out note with its owner cluster. Build root and owner-local Magma candidates by quark order from immediate unlinked ordinary leaves and floating notes. Prefix named note qualified identities with deployment_qnames(owner). Preserve attached-note hidden-link layout and exclude it from Magma. Thread the same cluster set through paint traversal so note-only owners cannot collapse later.
perturbation_axes: note before versus after ordinary leaves
two versus three standalone leaves across Magma's gate
acceptance: Every fresh evidence source is confirmed to dispatch as Diagram::Deployment.
A note-only owner renders as a cluster and its note is neither omitted nor emitted as a root leaf.
Owned floating notes join only their owner's Magma inventory; attached notes join no Magma inventory.
Nested owner, root stream, frame and solved-position inventories remain cardinality-consistent without panic or fallback.
Named notes use owner-qualified SVG identity and paint once.
An independent checker attacks depth, attachment, links, order, cardinality, direction and renamed labels at the exact implementation revision.
forbidden_approaches: adding note ids to DeploymentNode.children while consumers assume every child indexes DeploymentNode
filtering owned notes out of root paint without cluster registration
coordinate translations or SVG string reparenting after layout
treating every owned note as standalone
fixture aliases, filenames, coordinates, comparator or baseline changes
